This is the synopsis on Sister Claire website; "Rife with nuns, Witches, magick, werewolves, cats, giant robot mechas, and blue angels who pop out of toilets to announce approaching apocalypses, Sister Claire is the story of a young woman who leaves her quiet abbey to undergo a rigorous journey across a monster-riddled wilderness. On this journey, Claire begins to assemble the jigsaw puzzle of her past, present, and future, all while facing terrible dangers, finding new friends, and trying to save her found family from certain doom. Hot dog!" And man this web comic is a hoot to read! The pure absurdity (see woman coming out of toilet for example,) and adorableness are just two things that I love about Sister Claire. Along with her orange hair... And the kitties... And all the cameos, man there are a lot of cameos. It's so fun trying to spot them all. Book one covers Claire's life at the abbey and all the events that set forth her journey. While that may sound like a prolog it is a very much necessary story and essential to understand book 2 where the actual excursion into the wilderness takes place. A piece of advice, click on the new reader button on sister Claire's homepage, (link down below,) that will explain what missing moments are and gives some good info about Claire's world. Home page: https://www.sisterclaire.com/ Chapter list: https://www.sisterclaire.com/archive

This is the synopsis on Sister Claire website; "Rife with nuns, Witches, magick, werewolves, cats, giant robot mechas, and blue angels who pop out of toilets to announce approaching apocalypses, Sister Claire is the story of a young woman who leaves her quiet abbey to undergo a rigorous journey across a monster-riddled wilderness. On this journey, Claire begins to assemble the jigsaw puzzle of her past, present, and future, all while facing terrible dangers, finding new friends, and trying to save her found family from certain doom. Hot dog!" After the events of book 1, our favorite nuns are separated into two pairs; one group, the youngers of the kick-butt convent are journeying to a long gone promise land; while the other more mature, senior party track down their -- what they believe to be -- wayward friends. There is a lot of truths and secrets revealed, major character growth (in the junior and senior gals,) and most importantly-- more cameos! Seriously though, while cameos are fun it's the affection all of the characters share for one another, their understanding and willingness to do anything for each other is truly what this book is about. Such a great feel good story that will leave you wanting more. Home page: https://www.sisterclaire.com/ Chapter list: https://www.sisterclaire.com/archive

The beauty in a cold world. Book 3 starts out in an intense fight, blood was shed, and feathers fell as new characters enter the fray. While our best gals are being reacquainted with one another the birds swarm asking for help. Now that everything (okay most things) is out in the open, our girl Claire finally feels purpose in life and is spreading her figurative wings and exploring not only the world around her but also learning about the people that she cares for, and those that care for her, learning things that she could not even imagine. We've met some new friends along the way and with different factions coming to light the world of Sister Claire has grown exponentially in the series. I cannot get over how fun the series is even amid the heavier and more serious times, and things do take a darker turn in this book. The art has also improved exponentially, the panels are beautifully illustrated and the nature scenes are especially gorgeous. My favorite is the chapter nine cover. Every time I read it, I want to go out and explore the world around me and make new friends. Those good folks out there that are looking for magic too, that is. {Sparkles emoji} Home page: https://www.sisterclaire.com/ Chapter list: https://www.sisterclaire.com/archive (Insert shameless advertising here) Check out my bookstagram! @Witchy_Bookish_Otaku

Spinnerette was a blast to read. 3 1/2 stars **** To my knowledge Spinnerette was one of the first stories published by author Krazy Krow so some tweaking is to be expected, like how some of the scenes don't feel finished when they move on to the next and most panels don't give any evidence of scene changes as a warning. However, by the end things were moving much smoother and I'm sure they'll only get better from here. There were a lot of tongue-in-cheek gags and a bunch of references about different pop culture series and real life places giving the book a realistic feel, like there could be a (very secret) Super Hero Squad right in my hometown. I love the fact they're based out of Ohio, one state over from me. The characters are fun, realistic for them being superheroes, definitely diverse, and folks I could imagine grabbing a (boba) drink with. I am definitely looking forward to reading future volumes and can't wait to see what other hijinks they get into.

I... I did not expect that. The twist sucked me in. Once I started down that rabbit hole I was one and a half volumes down before I came up for air. And sadly I cannot share a bit of it or else that would be a major spoiler. The premise seems like it's a high school for superheroes vibe, but things get dark real fast. The dynamic between characters is fun to read. The art is nice, I like how the characters look like their powers in some way. For example, Seiya; His power is cryokinesis, the ability to generate and manipulate ice, like his ability, his looks are graceful and he can talk as smooth as ice, but like a frozen lake you must be careful not to venture too deep cause you don't know how deep or in his case, how shallow it is. The story is definitely intriguing and mysterious. I can't wait to see where it goes from here. I also get the idea that the, "Enemies of Humanity," are bit closer than most think.

Everyone has their own sound, you just have to find it. 3.5* stars After a great familial loss, Setsu also lost his sound, his "uniqueness", with his prized shamisen. To understand more of the world and find his sound once again, he leaves his small town and his brother for an adventure in Tokyo where he meets a kind girl who helps him along the away. Until the girl's, Yuna's, life also takes her away from Tokyo to better her career and find her own "sound," leaving Setsu her apartment and with no idea on what to do next. Within the first few pages I was hooked. Things moved at a good quick pace, which was good as by the middle of the book things jumped to a completely different scenario making the beginning feel like an elongated prolog or one shot. By the end I felt like I was reading a completely different book than I was at the beginning, the "first story" could have been told effectively in flashbacks in my opinion, and I did not like the feeling of a new story beginning at the last chapter and leaving me hanging. My issues with the pacing aside, I really do like the story being told in both parts of this volume, I would also like to see Yuna come back. The art is beautiful and illustrates music and the sound from the shamisen wonderfully. I would like to keep reading to see where this goes, hoping that things improve and can stay on a steadier track in following volumes. Check out my bookstagram! @Witchy.Otaku

Sweet and steamy beginning. Thank you to Netgalley and Media Do International for the free chapter one preview of Your Treacle Affects At Night in exchange for an honest review. The steaminess started right off the bat! (Nothing explicit though.) It got me hooked and I was sad when my chapter one was over. The art was simple with mostly straight, delicate lines that added a refreshing simplicity to the overall feel of the chapter. I also really like the short character bios and background info of the story (Including the names of manga also within this book's world) in this chapter and, I'm assuming, other characters that will show later in the book. Overall, there is nothing particularly special about the co-workers dating in secret trope here that one couldn't find elsewhere, however, I believe that there are some twists in store (twins?!) that could set this manga apart.

Steaminess ahead. Thank you to Netgalley and Media Do International for the free chapter one preview of My Beloved Lord in exchange for an honest review. If a ghost appears in your bedroom, don't offer to help complete its last wish to move on before you know what that wish is! Be glad Natsuki didn't know that tid-bit of info before he agreed to help Otono-sama, or else we wouldn't have this fun romp of a manga! Fair warning, this seems to be quite the steamy manga and not appropriate for younger readers, but for us adults who enjoy a bit of smut (yes, I said it) then read on, my fellow Yaoi lovers. The art was nice, giving a bubbly aesthetic to an already absurdly silly, Yaoi-centric storyline. It should be noted that Otono does try to force Natsuki to preform his last of 48 moves (a innocent one, unbeknownst to Natsuki,) to move on from this world, but Natsuki does a fine job of fending him off and only gives in when he feels bad for Otono… before knowing what was holding him back from moving on. This is definitely a book I'd like to read the rest of! It's something to tune out the world and just have a good time, I so wish I had more then just one chapter.
